name: Commonly Used Port
summary: Adversaries may communicate over a commonly used port to bypass firewalls or network detection systems and to blend in with normal network activity, to avoid more detailed inspection. They may use the protocol associated with the port, or a completely different protocol. They may use commonly open ports, such as the examples provided below. * TCP:80 (HTTP) * TCP:443 (HTTPS) * TCP/UDP:53 (DNS) * TCP:1024-4999 (OPC on XP/Win2k3) * TCP:49152-65535…

analytics.name: Analytic 1869
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) host or server establishing outbound connections on a commonly-allowed port (e.g., 443, 80, 8080, 53, etc.) to a destination not in the approved vendor/business domain list, where that host's documented network role does not require external connectivity. Documented real-world use: Sandworm's 2015 Ukraine power grid attack used port 443 for Command and Control (C2) communications. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where…

analytics.name: Analytic 2129
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux service process initiating an outbound connection on a commonly-used port to a destination not in the approved vendor domain list. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity.

analytics.name: Analytic 2221
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an embedded field device initiating outbound connections on a commonly-used port to a destination outside the device's documented operational communication profile, which for most embedded Industrial Control System (ICS) devices normally should not include arbitrary outbound internet connectivity under the approved communications architecture. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. analytics.name: Analytic 2271
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) vendor process making outbound connections on commonly-allowed port (e.g., 80, 443, 8080, etc.) to a destination not in the approved vendor domain list, from a host whose documented role does not require external connectivity. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity.
